**Every hidden file now carries its drive's key, locked with the password.**
A drive's folder has no header file any more: any single hidden file can be
recovered with just its drive's password, even if the rest of that drive is
gone. Copying files into a drive on Windows is also as fast as a plain copy.

> **Drives made by earlier versions don't open in this one.** If you have one
> with anything in it, copy the files out with v0.5.0 first (unlock it and
> copy them to an ordinary folder), then make a new drive, or convert that
> folder, with this version.

## Downloads

| Platform | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `cloak-v0.6.0-windows-x64.zip` | [WinFsp](https://winfsp.dev) (`winget install WinFsp.WinFsp`) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `cloak-v0.6.0-macos-arm64.dmg` | [macFUSE](https://macfuse.github.io) |

**Windows:** unzip and run `Cloak\Cloak.exe`. Keep the folder together: the
engine is in `Cloak\bin`, and your drive list and settings are kept in
`Cloak\cloak-data`.

**macOS:** open the disk image and drag **Cloak** onto **Applications**. The
app isn't notarized, so before opening it the first time, clear the download
quarantine: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Cloak.app` (or
right-click Cloak → Open, then Open again). macFUSE's kernel extension must be
allowed; on Apple Silicon that means its one-time Reduced Security setup.

## New

- **Recover a file with just its password.** A hidden file copied out of a
  drive, even one whose drive folder has since been deleted, can be brought
  into any other drive: **More → Bring in files from another drive…**, choose
  **Just its password (folder gone)**, and enter the password of the drive it
  came from.
- **Nothing in a drive's folder gives it away.** There's no header file, and
  the folder lists have ordinary-looking names that differ from drive to
  drive.
- **A lost top folder list is rebuilt.** The drive still unlocks from any of
  its files.

## Changed

- **Add existing drive** asks for the drive's password, since that's now the
  only thing that recognises a drive.
- **Change password** updates every file and folder in the drive (each carries
  the locked key), with a progress bar. If it's interrupted, opening the drive
  with the new password finishes it.
- **Back up** asks for each drive's password, and the backup holds the folder
  lists.

## Faster on Windows

- **Copying files into a drive** takes as long as a plain copy. In one test,
  16 files totalling 8.7 GB took 34 s, the same as a plain Windows copy
  (63 s before). Copies used to write every file to disk twice, and held its
  data in memory twice.
- **Creating many small files** is about 7 times faster.

## Fixed

- **A drive holding another drive's copied-in files** could end up opening
  only with that other drive's password. Each drive now opens only with its
  own; the copied files wait to be brought in.

## Known limitations

- Auto-lock runs on sleep, not when the screen locks.
- The app isn't code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run
  (More info → Run anyway).
- The middle of every file stays plaintext on disk by design.
- Hidden files of the same drive can be shown to belong together (they share
  the lock's salt); a file on its own looks random.
